nodes.label: Module 5 — Patient & Demographics (the patient spine)
nodes.rationale: The canonical identity of every person receiving hospice care and the spine every other clinical module hangs off; the bet is that precise, auditable identity hygiene is a real competitive advantage in survey readiness.

nodes.label: Patient Matching Pipeline (deterministic-first, probabilistic queued, D2)
nodes.rationale: Matches the IIS/EMPI consensus of deterministic + probabilistic + human review. Auto-merge is FORBIDDEN at any score because it creates the irreversible-merge class of disaster; tenant tuning is bounded (≥0.85 hard floor, ≤0.80 soft ceiling) so messy-intake agencies can adjust without code change.

nodes.label: PatientReader Seam (exactly six methods, D11)
nodes.rationale: Pinned to the six methods T-29.05's cascade needs — extra methods would tempt M29 into M5-shaped queries the dependency-cruiser forbids. Every result routes through patientResolver so merge-redirect is transparent, preventing bugs where a cascade returns the post-merge patient at L1 but the pre-merge patient at L4. 200ms p95 is a hard SLO.

nodes.label: PatientMutator Seam (field allowlist, SSN silently dropped, D12)
nodes.rationale: The mutator is the choke point enforcing 'ignore SSN even if the lab sends it' — defense in depth against PID-19 carrying sensitive identifiers from a chatty partner. MRN immutability prevents an external system rewriting M5's canonical identifier; status and merge transitions stay internal-only.

nodes.label: CaseloadProvider Seam (patient_assignment ∪ M17 active-shift visits, D4)
nodes.rationale: M3's caseload_membership ABAC needs a real provider and M5 is the only module with the primary-care-team truth; M17 contributes the on-shift reality. Boot validation refuses to start without registration — fail-loud at boot, never silent at runtime.

nodes.label: Append-Only Address History (D5)
nodes.rationale: Addresses carry compliance weight — state-Medicaid eligibility, Part 2 state overlay, RHC-vs-SNF place of service, routing geofence, §164.514 de-identification — so in-place UPDATE would lose prior state required for backdated audits.

nodes.label: PrivacyFlag Snapshot (M39 source of truth, deny-on-stale, D3)
nodes.rationale: A million reads a day cannot hit M39 each time (performance), a stale snapshot must never grant (safety), and every flip is an event recomputable from M39 history (auditability). A quarterly full rebuild reconciles drift.

nodes.label: §164.526 Right to Amend Workflow (60-day SLA, D9)
nodes.rationale: The HIPAA right is operational, not aspirational; the SLA alarm is the only thing that keeps it from quietly slipping, and the statement of disagreement is the deny path's required regulatory artifact that travels with every subsequent disclosure.

nodes.label: Merge via patient_resolver Redirect (reversible 30 days, D8)
nodes.rationale: Resolver-based redirect preserves audit referential integrity instead of destructively UPDATE-ing satellite tables; the 30-day reversibility window matches the typical 'we just realized' lag, and restricting late unmerge to platform break-glass keeps it from becoming routine.

nodes.label: Selective Envelope Encryption (SSN + state ID only, D6)
nodes.rationale: Minimum-necessary encryption surface: encryption applies where the column would otherwise be a privacy-impact magnet. MBI is the non-sensitive Medicare surrogate and stays plaintext; over-encryption breaks search and joins without compensating risk reduction.
